explication:
<explanation>
1. Project Type and Purpose  
   - This is not a traditional full-stack web app but a browser user-script extension (“VOT”) that runs in Tampermonkey (or similar) to inject voice-over translation and subtitles into arbitrary video pages (YouTube, other sites).  
   - The README emphasizes features like on-the-fly translation (via Yandex.Translate or proxy), subtitle display & saving, audio export, UI customization, volume sync, and multi-language support.

2. Key Architectural Components  
   a. Development & CI  
      - GitHub repository with CI workflows (.github/workflows/build.yml, release.yml).  
      - Linting/precommit via Husky, ESLint, Prettier.  
      - Patch-package workflows for vendored dependency fixes (patches/).  
      - Localization generation tool (scripts/wiki-gen and @toil/localize-tui).  
      - Tests folder.  
   b. Build & Distribution  
      - Build scripts in package.json (npm run build, build:min, etc.).  
      - Output artifacts in dist/ (vot.user.js, vot-min.user.js).  
      - Dependencies managed via npm or Bun (bun.lock, package-lock.json).  
   c. Runtime (Injected User Script)  
      - src/index.js: entry point registered as user script.  
      - Core modules under src/:  
         • config (config.js)  
         • localization (hashes.json, locales, provider)  
         • ui (ui.js, ui/tooltip.ts) and styles (SCSS under src/styles)  
         • subtitle orchestration (subtitles.js)  
         • utilities (VideoObserver, storage, translateApis, volume control, errors)  
      - Type definitions (global.d.ts, index.d.ts, tooltip.ts).  
   d. External Services  
      - Yandex.Translate API (direct or via proxy servers)  
      - Proxy servers (vot-worker, media-proxy) for CORS or media-format support  
      - VOT-Backend for unsupported video formats  
      - Supported site pages (YouTube, others) where script is injected  

3. Drawing the System Diagram  
   - Use a layered diagram with these zones:  
     1. Developer/CI Layer  
        • GitHub repo → CI workflows → Build & Release  
     2. Build Pipeline Layer  
        • Source code (src/) + patches/ + scripts/ + localization tool → Bundler (npm build) → dist/ artifacts  
     3. Runtime Layer (User’s Browser)  
        • Tampermonkey (MV2/MV3) loads dist/vot.user.js  
        • Script Initialization (index.js)  
        • Modules:  
           - Config & Feature Flags  
           - Localization Provider → locale JSON  
           - UI Components (menu, sliders, tooltip) + SCSS styles  
           - VideoObserver → hook into HTMLVideoElement  
           - TranslateAPI Adapter → direct or via Proxy Servers  
           - Subtitles Manager → render, save, sync  
           - Audio Mixer → capture translation audio, sync volume  
           - Storage (localStorage or indexedDB) for saving settings/subtitles  
        • Interaction with Host Page DOM & Video Element  
     4. External Services Layer  
        • Yandex.Translate Server  
        • Proxy Servers (vot-worker, media-proxy)  
        • VOT-Backend Service  

4. Relationships & Data Flows  
   - Arrows from the Script → Host Page (DOM injection & event listeners)  
   - VideoObserver → passes frames/time events → Subtitles Manager → UI overlay  
   - TranslateAPI Adapter → (arrow) → Yandex.Translate or Proxy → returns text/audio  
   - Audio Mixer → injects <audio> element or AudioContext → output mixed track  
   - UI Controls → user actions (volume slider, language select) → Config & Storage  
   - Build Pipeline → produces user script → deployed via GitHub Releases  

5. Architectural Patterns & Principles  
   - Modular separation (config / localization / UI / utils)  
   - Single Responsibility per module (VideoObserver only watches player events, TranslateApis only handles API calls, etc.)  
   - Adapter pattern for translation backends (direct vs. proxy vs. backend)  
   - Observer pattern for video time updates & UI refresh  
   - Plugin-style localization (load JSON bundles)  
   - Build-time patch integration via patch-package  

6. Tailoring the Diagram for a User-Script Project  
   - Focus on content-script execution environment (no server-side code resides here).  
   - Emphasize injection points into third-party pages.  
   - Highlight external translation services and CORS/proxy workarounds.  
   - Show build/test/localization toolchain separately from runtime.  

7. Diagramming Guidelines  
   - Use clear rectangular boxes for components (e.g., “VideoObserver”, “TranslateAPI Adapter”, “UI Module”).  
   - Group related modules (src/config + src/localization under “Core Libraries”, src/ui + src/styles under “Presentation”).  
   - Draw directional arrows to depict data flows: e.g., Video time → Subtitles Manager → UI Overlay; User clicks → Config → Storage.  
   - Color-code boxes by layer:  
      • Blue for Build & CI  
      • Green for Runtime Modules  
      • Orange for External Services  
   - Use dashed lines for optional/proxy paths (e.g., direct API vs. proxy server).  
   - Label arrows with method names or data types (e.g., “GET /translate”, “onTimeUpdate”).  

8. Capture Essential Details  
   - Be explicit about the injection environment (Tampermonkey host context).  
   - Illustrate how localization is loaded at startup.  
   - Show how SCSS styles compile into inline `<style>` or imported CSS.  
   - Represent the patch-package mechanism at build time.  
   - Don’t omit the script’s interplay with browser storage and page DOM.  
   - Detail the external proxy/back-end services enabling translation and media handling.  

By following this layered, modular diagram approach—with clear labels, color-coding, and directional arrows—you’ll produce a precise architectural overview that captures both the build-time toolchain and the runtime workflow of the VOT user-script project.  
</explanation>
